_comment: ORACLE rung of the varying-rule axis: rule EXECUTION isolated from rule
INDUCTION.
subst-fst-oracle states the map outright in the prompt (`MAP a->c b->a
c->b`) while the demos, targets and scoring are unchanged from subst-fst.
So the two rungs differ only in whether the rule must be INFERRED from the
demos or is TOLD in the prompt:
oracle scores, subst-fst does not  ->  execution works, induction does not
neither scores                    ->  cannot execute a stated rule at all
both score                        ->  induction works
This is the sharpest single experiment available on this task, and it needs
no new code. It has not been run: every number so far is on the
weights-only rung or the induction rung, so 'the model cannot induce a rule'
and 'the model cannot apply a rule at all' have never been told apart.
Read with all three instruments: byte accuracy vs target, byte accuracy vs
query, and off_pair rate (chance 0.333 on a 3-symbol alphabet). Held-out
below chance on all three means the output is a uniform draw; off_pair is
the one that cannot be gamed by a positional bias.
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep -- \
research/experiments/varying-rule-oracle.json data gpu 16 48 128 288 --seeds=0,1,2
k_set is [1,2,3,5] with k0_rate 0, matching data-axis-varying-rule.json
exactly, so the ONLY difference between the two runs is the oracle header.
